issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires Farm to hold its animals in a List and to initialize that List as an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation instead declares the animals attribute as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. This changes the exposed type of getAnimals()/setAnimals() (Queue vs. expected List) and the concrete collection used (LinkedList vs. requested ArrayList). Students instructed to use List/ArrayList will be confused by the solution's Queue/LinkedList choice and any tests that check for the List type or an ArrayList initialization may fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem specification: change the animals field to use List<Animal> (private List<Animal> animals;), initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor (this.animals = new ArrayList<>();), and update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Queue/LinkedList was intentional, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a Queue and LinkedList so students are not instructed to use List/ArrayList.
